open.why: TWO of the three doors B1 named are closed; the THIRD is not. Closed: the reviewer's own scripts, re-run verbatim on the branch tip (PGPORT=55508 clara_649, live body confirmed CLIENT-first by pg_get_functiondef) — lockorder.mjs now gives `X result: CLR10 client onboarding is not open` / settle ok (client row 6/30) and lockorder-commit.mjs the same, where both previously gave 40P01; my own honest reverse race (a REAL cancel door in flight and blocked on the plan lock, then a CLEAN settle transaction — the only shape PostgREST can produce, and settle has ZERO internal callers: `grep settle_client_onboarding_facts packages/db/migrations/*.sql` matches only 0204) drains without a deadlock, and 12 simultaneous real settle-vs-cancel/commit pairs gave `ok/CLR10` twelve times, zero 40P01 (C:\Users\zhant\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\649rc\lockorder-honest.mjs). lockorder-rev.mjs verbatim still prints 40P01, but its premise is now STALE — its R1 hand-locks the plan row in the settle transaction, which the fixed door no longer does. STILL OPEN: approve_opening_seed, the third door B1's own text names ('0017:3856 advisory 203005004 then 0017:3857 plan FOR UPDATE'). The fix moved only the ROW locks; settle still reaches the CLIENT's advisory rung 203005004 inside clara.set_client_fy_end, i.e. AFTER its plan row lock (live def: advisoryIdx 1643 < updateIdx 4372 inside set_client_fy_end, which settle calls at 0204:552). So settle: plan-row -> client-rung; approve_opening_seed: client-rung -> plan-row. Proven on the ticket rig with the reviewer's own methodology (Tx X performs approve_opening_seed's OWN two acquisitions): C:\...\649rc\advrung.mjs -> `X result: 40P01`; advrung2.mjs sweeps the interleaving and at delay=150/300/600ms the SETTLE door is the victim — `settle=40P01 deadlock detected` with `client={"fy_end_month":null,"fy_end_day":null}`, i.e. exactly B1's failure mode (the accounting write dies with an untyped error the web door has no face for). Not a regression — this leg was already open at baaf48fe (settle has always called set_client_fy_end after the plan lock). FIX: take the rung immediately after the client ROW lock and before the plan lock — `perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(203005004, hashtext(v_client::text));` — advisory xact locks are re-entrant (0037:2526-2528 says so), so set_client_fy_end re-taking it later is free, commit/cancel take no rung at all so nothing inverts, and settle then matches approve_opening_seed's rung-before-plan order. Extend p649.settle.lock_order with an approve_opening_seed-shaped adversary.

new_blockers.what: The B1 fix introduced a CROSS-TENANT row lock, and the migration's own comment states the opposite as fact. 0204:485-492 promises 'A plan that does not exist, or belongs to another firm, yields NULL and locks nothing … with no existence oracle', but the pre-read it describes (`select op.client_id into v_client from clara.onboarding_plans op where op.id = p_plan`, 0204:499) carries NO firm predicate and the function is SECURITY DEFINER, so a foreign plan yields a REAL client_id and the next line takes `clara.clients … FOR UPDATE` on another firm's row — before the CLR11 firm check. Measured on the lane rig (C:\Users\zhant\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\649rc\crosstenant2.mjs, PGPORT=55508 clara_649): firm-B admin settling firm-A's plan while firm A holds its OWN client row → `CLR11 plan_not_in_firm after 2453ms`; control with the row free → `after 51ms`. The SAME probe against the PRE-fix body (55608/clara_649r, before I re-applied 0204 there; checkfn reported `order=PLAN-FIRST (unfixed)`) → `after 7ms` with the row locked. So the wait is new in this fix round: an unauthorized caller now queues on another tenant's row and can time the difference, in a door whose own text cites 0021's no-existence-oracle rule. Severity note for the orchestrator: no data is disclosed, no refusal changes and the foreign lock is released microseconds later when CLR11 aborts the transaction — this is a tenant-isolation/contract-honesty defect, not a data-loss one; it is filed here because the estate treats tenant isolation as a top-line property and the remedy is one predicate.
new_blockers.fix: Scope the pre-read to the caller's firm: `select op.client_id into v_client from clara.onboarding_plans op where op.id = p_plan and op.firm_id = c.firm;`. A foreign or unknown plan then yields NULL, locks nothing, and the existing `select * into p … for update` still raises the same CLR11 plan_not_in_firm with no oracle; for legitimate calls the CLIENT-before-PLAN order and the plan_client_moved belt are unchanged. Correct the 0204 comment to match, and add a cell asserting a foreign-firm settle refuses CLR11 in constant time while the target firm holds its own client row (the current battery has no cross-tenant timing cell — p649.settle.replay_isolation only races settle against settle).
